profiles.declaredVsObserved: Declared no-first-use (2016 party congress) was quietly abandoned by the 2022 law's enumerated non-nuclear first-use conditions, and the 2018 Singapore denuclearisation pledge was followed by continued missile development — so declaratory restraint carries near-zero information about behaviour in this actor. The sharpest live divergence is the "automatic and immediate" retaliation language sitting against assessed sole personal release authority: one of the two is theatre, most likely the automaticity, and the model should carry both branches rather than resolve them.

authority.statement: Go/no-go on strategic action sits in a single office at the apex of both party and state — designated in law since September 2022 as the President of the State Affairs, who holds all decisive powers over the nuclear forces, and who since the January 2021 Rules revision chairs the Party Central Military Commission as General Secretary. No subordinate body has been observed reversing a decision taken in that office; the bodies below it prepare, ratify and codify.
authority.basis: DECLARED and OBSERVED, converging. The 2013 Law on Consolidating the Position of a Nuclear Weapons State (1 Apr 2013) vested release authority in the 'Supreme Commander of the KPA'; the 2022 Law on the State Policy on the Nuclear Forces (7th Session of the 14th Supreme People's Assembly, 8 Sep 2022) moved it to the 'President of State Affairs' — Jun Bong-geun, 'Comparing North Korea's Law on Nuclear Forces Policy (2022) with the Law on Consolidating the Position of Nuclear Weapons State (2013)', Asia-Pacific Leadership Network commentary, 21 Nov 2022. The chairmanship link is clause-level: Hisashi Hirai (Kyodo News), 'On the Revisions to the Rules of the Workers' Party of Korea', Japan Institute of International Affairs Research Report, 9 Sep 2021, records that the revised Rules make the General Secretary chairman of the Party Central Military Commission and strengthen that Commission's authority. DIA, North Korea Military Power (DIA-02-1801-056, 2021), assesses assertive, personally held national and nuclear command and control. CAVEAT ON THE DIA CITE: the parent profile records that the DIA PDF returned 403 in its challenge session, and it could not be retrieved in this review either; specific page references carried in an earlier draft have been removed rather than repeated unverified, and the report is cited here at document level only.

steps.stage: Line-setting and resourcing — the strategic programme against which every later proposal is justified
steps.office: Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea and the plenary meetings of its Central Committee
steps.gate: Stops what nobody has resourced, not what the leadership has willed. A proposal that cannot be attached to the announced line has no budget line and no bureaucratic sponsor; a proposal the apex office wants proceeds whether or not the line anticipated it. Model this as a filter on the routine choice set and not as a veto.
steps.basis: The Eighth Congress (5-12 Jan 2021) adopted a five-year national defence development plan enumerating specific systems — tactical nuclear warheads, solid-propellant ICBMs, a military reconnaissance satellite, multiple warheads, a nuclear-powered submarine. 38 North, 'Assessing North Korea's Five-Year Effort to Develop 13 New Nuclear and Missile Systems' (Jan 2026), tracks delivery against that list system by system. The April 2018 'new strategic line' plenum is the same mechanism running in the restraint direction (see history). Hirai/JIIA (9 Sep 2021) records the Rules change fixing Congresses at five-year intervals.

steps.stage: Staff plan development — operational planning and technical readiness, by lane
steps.office: KPA General Staff Department (conventional and border action)
steps.gate: Technical feasibility and readiness only. This stage demonstrably does not gate permission: in June 2020 the General Staff announced a four-point action plan and preparations for at least part of it had begun before the ratifying body met. Treat this as constraining timing and options, not authorisation.
steps.basis: June 2020 sequence: 38 North, 'Kim Jong Un Puts Anti-South Korea Military Operation on Hold. What Now?' (25 Jun 2020), notes the plan was 'reported as subject to ratification by the CMC' while 'preparations had already begun for at least the leaflet campaign before this CMC preliminary meeting was held.' RGB subordination of cyber operations: CISA/State/Treasury/FBI Alert AA20-106A, 'Guidance on the North Korean Cyber Threat' (rev. 23 Jun 2020); DOJ, '3 North Korean Military Hackers Indicted…' (C.D. Cal., unsealed 17 Feb 2021), which charges the defendants as members of RGB units. Munitions Industry Department subordination of the Nuclear Weapons Institute and Academy of Defence Sciences: North Korea Leadership Watch (M. Madden), 'MID-le Managers', 13 Sep 2024. CAVEAT: the internal reporting lines of the MID complex rest on sanctions listings, defector-derived reporting and analyst reconstruction, not on published DPRK organisational documents. Authority chain as researched: Reconnaissance General Bureau (clandestine, foreign and cyber operations); Munitions Industry Department of the WPK Central Committee, with the Missile Administration, Nuclear Weapons Institute, Academy of Defence Sciences and Second Academy of Natural Sciences subordinate to it (systems development)

steps.stage: Party political vetting — loyalty and cadre control over the officers who would execute
steps.office: Organization and Guidance Department of the WPK Central Committee
steps.gate: Removes people, not plans. General-officer appointments require Organization and Guidance Department sign-off before the supreme commander's appointment order issues, and political officers are seated in KPA units down to company level. Its practical effect on the model is that proposals rarely reach the apex office carrying institutional dissent — so an engine should not expect bureaucratic friction to attenuate a decision here.
steps.basis: North Korea Leadership Watch, 'KPA General Political Bureau' entity file, and GlobalSecurity.org, 'General Political Bureau — North Korea', both describing the Bureau as operating under the Central Military Commission's direction while its activities are directed by the Organization and Guidance Department, and describing OGD approval as a precondition for appointments above brigadier general. Michael Madden, 'North Korea Reiterates Party's Precedence Over the Military, Conducts Sweeping Changes in KPA Leadership', 38 North, 31 Jul 2025, records a Central Military Commission meeting on 'exercising tight control and guidance so that all military and political activities of the DPRK armed forces are thoroughly conducted as required by the Party's military line', and the dispatch of political commissars afterwards. General authoritarian-control toolkit: D. Byman & J. Lind, 'Pyongyang's Survival Strategy', International Security 35(1), 2010. CAVEAT: the rank threshold and the surveillance-reporting mechanics come from defector-derived accounts relayed through secondary compilations; the existence and direction of the control relationship is much better attested than its procedural detail. Authority chain as researched: working through the General Political Bureau of the Korean People's Army and its commissar network

steps.stage: Ratification of a prepared military action, or formal legitimation of one already ordered
steps.office: Central Military Commission of the WPK Central Committee
steps.gate: The only institutional body observed stopping a prepared DPRK military action. On 23 June 2020 a preliminary meeting for the Fifth Meeting of the Seventh Central Military Commission suspended — deferred, explicitly not cancelled — the General Staff's four-point plan against the ROK. The same body also issues after-the-fact legitimation: the Kursk deployment entered the domestic record through an unusual Central Military Commission 'written stand' on 28 April 2025. Because the apex office chairs this Commission, 'ratification' here should not be scored as an independent check.
steps.basis: KCNA report of 24 Jun 2020 on the 23 Jun preliminary CMC meeting, as reported by AP/Washington Post ('N. Korea: Kim suspended military retaliation against South', 23-24 Jun 2020) and analysed in 38 North (25 Jun 2020). April 2025: 38 North, 'North Korea's Acknowledgement of War Participation' (Apr 2025), which describes the 'written stand' of the Central Military Commission as a highly unusual instrument chosen for a sensitive military issue. Chairmanship: Hirai/JIIA (9 Sep 2021). NOTE ON DIRECTION OF EVIDENCE: one documented stop is one data point. It shows the gate exists; it does not establish how often it is used.

steps.stage: Release decision — the irreversible go/no-go on strategic use
steps.office: Office of the President of the State Affairs and Supreme Commander of the armed forces
steps.gate: Sole authority, with no observed reversal from below. The supporting command organisation the 2022 law creates is assessed in the open literature as nominal, so the engine should not model it as a second signature. This is the step that produces `decisionCentralization` at 0.94 and the high behavioural variance that goes with a single decider.
steps.basis: 2013 and 2022 nuclear laws as analysed in Jun Bong-geun, APLN, 21 Nov 2022, which describes the 2022 law's supporting body as 'very nominal' and notes that command still belongs to one office; and in A. Barannikova, 'Nuclear Strategy of the DPRK: Doctrine Evolution and Future Prospects', NAPSNet Special Report, Nautilus Institute, 15 Mar 2024. DIA, North Korea Military Power (2021), cited at document level only — see the caveat on `authority`. DECLARATORY TENSION TO CARRY, not resolve: the 2022 law's 'automatic and immediate' retaliation clause for an attack on the leadership or on the nuclear command organisation sits against sole personal release authority. One of the two is theatre; the parent profile judges the automaticity the more likely candidate, and this dossier does not improve on that. Authority chain as researched: nominally assisted by the 'state nuclear forces command organisation' created by the 2022 law

steps.stage: Legal and constitutional formalisation — codifying a decision already taken
steps.office: Supreme People's Assembly and its Presidium
steps.gate: None in practice. This body has not been observed amending or refusing a leadership-originated measure; it converts decisions into law, and the act of codification is itself part of the signal. An engine that credits this stage with delay or veto probability will mispredict tempo.
steps.basis: The nuclear-use law was adopted at the 7th Session of the 14th Supreme People's Assembly on 8 Sep 2022 (Jun Bong-geun, APLN, 21 Nov 2022; Japan Institute of International Affairs, 'North Korea's Supreme People's Assembly Adopts Nuclear Use Law', research report, Jan 2023). The Law on Rejecting Reactionary Thought and Culture was adopted by the SPA Presidium on 4 Dec 2020 and revised 19 Aug 2022; the state never published the text, which was obtained and analysed outside the country (Daily NK, 'Daily NK acquires full text of the anti-reactionary thought law'). The same non-publication pattern applies to the October 2024 constitutional revision, per 38 North, 'Paving the Way for Hostile Coexistence? What North Korea's Constitutional Revisions Mean for Inter-Korean Ties' (May 2026). That pattern is itself the finding: codification is real, publication is selective, and analysts work from excerpts and obtained copies.

steps.stage: Execution and the attribution decision — whether the act is claimed
steps.office: State media apparatus of the WPK Central Committee - KCNA and Rodong Sinmun - in the overt lane
steps.gate: Decides only whether the institution's hand is shown, and it is the stage that manufactures the profile's bimodality. Missile launches, artillery action and force deployments are announced, photographed and dated; cryptocurrency theft and IT-worker placement have never been acknowledged and run behind front companies and laundered identities. A single `attributionAversion` scalar averages across this gate and therefore describes no behaviour the institution has actually shown.
steps.basis: OVERT LANE: state-media announcement is the norm — e.g. the KPA Strategic Force's published Guam plan (Aug 2017) and the Central Military Commission's written acknowledgement of the Kursk deployment (28 Apr 2025, per 38 North). COVERT LANE: the FBI attributed roughly $1.5B stolen from Bybit on or about 21 Feb 2025 to DPRK activity it tracks as 'TraderTraitor' (FBI Public Service Announcement, 26 Feb 2025); the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team's report of 22 Oct 2025 documents front-company use and identity laundering. The DPRK has acknowledged none of it. CAVEAT: an earlier draft named the Propaganda and Agitation Department of the WPK Central Committee as the office owning this decision; no source consulted documents that attribution, so it has been removed and the office named here is restricted to the publication channels the sources actually show (KCNA and Rodong Sinmun). The lane split is well evidenced; which body inside the Central Committee decides the claim is not. Authority chain as researched: no acknowledging office at all in the covert revenue and intelligence lane

tempo.statement: Two clocks that must not be averaged. Programme decisions run on multi-decade continuity punctuated by five-year plans; crisis decisions run on days. In the two best-documented crisis sequences the interval from a staff proposal becoming public to a decision being announced was five to six days.
tempo.basis: CRISIS CLOCK: Aug 2017 — KPA Strategic Force statement 9-10 Aug, decision to hold announced 15 Aug (five to six days). Jun 2020 — General Staff four-point plan announced 17 Jun, Central Military Commission suspension 23 Jun, reported 24 Jun (six to seven days). PROGRAMME CLOCK: the Eighth Congress five-year defence development plan of Jan 2021, tracked against thirteen systems by 38 North (Jan 2026); nuclear effort sustained from the 1950s to declared irreversible status in 2022-23. COMPRESSING PRESSURE: Ju Hyung Kim, 'North Korea's Emerging Limited Nuclear-Use Strategy', Global Security Review, 2026, argues that ROK Three-Axis/Kill Chain posture creates incentives to shorten decision times further. LOAD-BEARING CAVEAT: both crisis cases with a clean public timeline are cases where the institution chose to HOLD. There is no comparably documented proposal-to-execution interval for a case where it chose to act, so this figure measures deliberation under scrutiny, not reaction speed, and an engine should not use it as a strike-timeline estimate.

preconditions.statement: The action can be attached to the strategic line announced at the last Congress or Central Committee plenum. Routine capability development is justified against that list; deviations require the apex office to sponsor them directly.
preconditions.basis: The Eighth Congress (Jan 2021) five-year defence development plan enumerated the systems subsequently pursued, tracked item by item in 38 North, 'Assessing North Korea's Five-Year Effort to Develop 13 New Nuclear and Missile Systems' (Jan 2026). The mechanism runs in the restraint direction too: the Third Plenary Meeting of the Seventh Central Committee (20 Apr 2018) announced a 'new strategic line' and the test suspension in the same report (KCNA text as republished by the National Committee on North Korea).

preconditions.statement: A capability is demonstrated before it is used as leverage. Declaratory claims follow tests and displays rather than preceding them, so a demand backed by an undemonstrated capability is off-pattern for this institution.
preconditions.basis: OBSERVED PATTERN, not a stated rule. The 2006 test was preceded by a public statement of intent six days earlier; the 'completion of the state nuclear force' declaration followed the November 2017 Hwasong-15 flight rather than anticipating it; systems named in the 2021 five-year plan were tested and paraded before appearing in declaratory framing (38 North, Jan 2026). CAVEAT: this is an inference from sequence across a modest number of cases and no DPRK document states it.

preconditions.statement: Covert-lane action presupposes standing laundering and identity infrastructure. Front companies, stolen and fabricated identities, and placed IT workers are maintained as persistent capacity, so the covert lane's lead time sits in the infrastructure rather than in the operation.
preconditions.basis: Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (11 nations), 'The DPRK's Violation and Evasion of UN Sanctions through Cyber and Information Technology Worker Activities', 22 Oct 2025, documenting identity laundering and front-company use at scale. The pattern is older than the report: the DOJ complaint unsealed 6 Sep 2018 describes a programmer operating through a DPRK government front company across the 2014 Sony intrusion, the 2016 Bangladesh Bank theft and the 2017 WannaCry outbreak.

preconditions.statement: Enforcement cover from a Security Council patron lowers the expected cost of overt action, and the institution has moved at higher tempo when that cover was in place.
preconditions.basis: ASSUMED, NOT DEMONSTRATED — flagged because it is tempting and thin. The UN 1718 Panel of Experts mandate lapsed in April 2024 on a Russian veto and the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team was stood up outside the UN as a substitute (MSMT, 22 Oct 2025). The Russia treaty, the troop deployment and the 2024-25 escalation in cryptocurrency theft all follow. That is a correlation across a single period with an obvious confound (the same partnership supplies both the veto and the demand for troops), and no source consulted establishes the causal direction. Do not let an engine treat this as a trigger condition.

afterAction.statement: The institution acknowledges and rapidly re-attempts technical failure in the overt lane, adapts tactically to costly outcomes without treating cost as grounds to stop, and acknowledges nothing at all in the covert lane. Learning is visible; reversal is not.
afterAction.basis: OVERT TECHNICAL FAILURE: state media announced the failure of the 31 May 2023 Chollima-1 satellite launch within hours, naming low reliability of the new engine system and unstable fuel, and the programme re-attempted in August and November 2023 (CNBC and SpaceNews, 31 May 2023; CSIS Beyond Parallel, 'Another Failed Satellite Launch at the Sohae Satellite Launching Station'). COSTLY OPERATIONS: 38 North, 'North Korea's Military Intervention in Kursk: A High Casualty Learning Curve' (Feb 2025), documents tactical adaptation after heavy infantry losses, followed by further rotations rather than withdrawal; UK Defence Intelligence assessed roughly 6,000 casualties from about 11,000 deployed by June 2025 (Bloomberg, 16 Jun 2025) while ROK assessments earlier in 2025 put the figure nearer 4,000 with roughly 3,000 reinforcements sent in January-February — a spread the model should carry rather than resolve. COVERT: no DPRK acknowledgement of any attributed cyber operation, including the Bybit theft (FBI PSA, 26 Feb 2025). GAP TO STATE PLAINLY: no open source consulted documents an internal review process, a lessons-learned mechanism, or an accountability outcome; what is observable is the behaviour after failure, not the procedure that produced it.

declaredEnds.statement: Continuity of the governing authority as a sovereign, independent state under the existing leadership is the first-order objective, ahead of economic, diplomatic and territorial goals.
declaredEnds.basis: DIA, North Korea Military Power (DIA-02-1801-056, 2021), states the first objective of national security strategy as ensuring the regime's long-term security, defined as remaining a sovereign, independent country under the existing leadership. This is the declared end that underwrites the `regime-continuity` redline in the parent profile. CAVEAT: the source PDF returned 403 in the parent profile's challenge session and could not be retrieved in this review either; the page cite carried in an earlier draft has been removed and the report is cited at document level only.

declaredEnds.statement: The Party's stated immediate goal is building a wealthy and civilised socialist society in the northern half of the Republic, with a communist society as the final goal; the clause on carrying out a 'National Liberation Democratic Revolution' was deleted in the January 2021 Rules revision.
declaredEnds.basis: Hisashi Hirai, 'On the Revisions to the Rules of the Workers' Party of Korea', JIIA Research Report, 9 Sep 2021 — a clause-level reading of the Rules as revised at the Eighth Congress (5-12 Jan 2021). The deletion matters for modelling because it removes a declared revolutionary claim on the counterpart Korean state's territory from the Party's own statement of purpose, three years before the 'two hostile states' turn made the same move at state level. CAVEAT: the DPRK does not publish the full Rules text; clause-level analyses rest on state-media excerpts and copies obtained abroad.

declaredEnds.statement: Retention of nuclear weapons is declared an accomplished and irreversible condition of the state rather than an objective still being negotiated toward.
declaredEnds.basis: DECLARED: the 2022 Law on the State Policy on the Nuclear Forces (8 Sep 2022) and the September 2023 constitutional amendment enshrining nuclear force policy, framed by the leadership as making the status irreversible; the 2022 law also deleted the 2013 law's disarmament and international-cooperation clauses (Jun Bong-geun, APLN, 21 Nov 2022; A. Barannikova, NAPSNet Special Report, Nautilus Institute, 15 Mar 2024). OBSERVED: consistent with the 2019 Hanoi refusal recorded below.

declaredEnds.statement: A five-year national defence development programme with enumerated deliverables — tactical nuclear warheads, solid-propellant ICBMs, multiple warheads, a military reconnaissance satellite, a nuclear-powered submarine — adopted as a published plan rather than an aspiration.
declaredEnds.basis: Eighth Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea, 5-12 Jan 2021. Delivery tracked system by system in 38 North, 'Assessing North Korea's Five-Year Effort to Develop 13 New Nuclear and Missile Systems' (Jan 2026); corroborating survey in the CRS In Focus product on North Korea's nuclear weapons and missile programs (IF10472) and SIPRI Yearbook chapter on North Korean nuclear forces.

declaredEnds.statement: Since December 2023 unification is no longer a declared end: the counterpart Korean state is officially characterised as a separate and hostile state rather than as a part of one nation to be reunified.
declaredEnds.basis: December 2023 Central Committee plenum 'two hostile states' formulation and the October 2024 constitutional revision reportedly removing reunification and 'northern half' formulations, analysed in Columbia Korean Legal Studies, 'The Order to "Erase" Unification and the "Hostile State" Revision'. CAVEAT carried from the parent profile: 38 North, 'Paving the Way for Hostile Coexistence? What North Korea's Constitutional Revisions Mean for Inter-Korean Ties' (May 2026), records that the full constitutional text was never published, so the direction of travel is well supported and the clause-level detail is not.

selfImage.statement: The institution presents itself as a full-fledged and 'responsible' nuclear weapons state exercising lawful self-defence as a sovereign equal — legally entitled to the capability, procedurally correct in acquiring it, and wronged rather than delinquent in being sanctioned for it.
selfImage.basis: DECLARED, and legible in the form of its own documents rather than only their content. The 2013 statute is titled a Law on Consolidating the Position of a Nuclear Weapons State; the 2003 withdrawal from the NPT was executed through formal Article X notice and framed in the accompanying government statement (KCNA, 10 Jan 2003) as a legitimate self-defensive measure; Article 4 of the 2024 treaty with Russia invokes UN Charter Article 51 by name (CRS In Focus IF12760, 'Russia-North Korea Relations'). The parent profile's `legitimacyWeight` of 0.28 should be read against this: the discount is on external APPROVAL, not on external LEGITIMATION, which the institution invests in consistently.

threatModel.statement: United States 'hostile policy', extended-deterrence assets, and US-ROK combined exercises, which it characterises as offensive and confrontational irrespective of their declared defensive framing.
threatModel.basis: DECLARED, and stated with high consistency across years. KCNA year-end characterisation of US military activity in the region as 'gravely threatening' to strategic stability (reported in Stars and Stripes, 28 Nov 2025). Two further items carried in an earlier draft - a KCNA commentary quoted as saying exercises 'cannot conceal their inherently offensive and confrontational nature', and a DPRK objection to eleven-nation UN Command participation in Freedom Shield - carried no date, outlet or document identifier and could not be located in this review; they have been removed rather than repeated. Confidence is high that this is the DECLARED threat model; it carries no claim about whether the institution's internal assessment matches its declaratory one.

threatModel.statement: Decapitation of the leadership or of the nuclear command organisation, which it has written into statute as a categorical trigger rather than treating as one contingency among many.
threatModel.basis: DECLARED: the 2022 Law on the State Policy on the Nuclear Forces names attack on the state leadership and on the command organisation of the nuclear forces as conditions for automatic and immediate nuclear response (Jun Bong-geun, APLN, 21 Nov 2022; Barannikova, Nautilus, 15 Mar 2024). Driver on the other side: Ju Hyung Kim, 'North Korea's Emerging Limited Nuclear-Use Strategy', Global Security Review, 2026, on ROK Three-Axis/Kill Chain posture. NEVER TESTED — this is the single most consequential untested declaration in the profile, and the parent profile marks the corresponding redline low-confidence for that reason.

threatModel.statement: Internal ideological and informational penetration, treated as a security threat serious enough to legislate against with criminal penalties, not merely as a propaganda problem.
threatModel.basis: DECLARED via statute: the Law on Rejecting Reactionary Thought and Culture, adopted by the Supreme People's Assembly Presidium on 4 Dec 2020 and revised 19 Aug 2022, four chapters and 41 articles, with graduated penalties for consuming and for distributing foreign — principally ROK — cultural material. The state never published the text; the analysis rests on a copy obtained outside the country (Daily NK, 'Daily NK acquires full text of the anti-reactionary thought law', and Daily NK's October 2024 study of the law's social effect). Broader survival-toolkit framing: Byman & Lind, International Security 35(1), 2010. CAVEAT: penalty ranges reported in secondary sources vary and derive from the obtained text plus defector testimony; confidence is low on specifics and higher on the existence and direction of the measure.

threatModel.statement: Trilateral US-Japan-ROK military alignment, treated as consolidation of encirclement rather than as three separate bilateral relationships.
threatModel.basis: DECLARED: DPRK statements condemning trilateral US-Japan-ROK drills as dangerous and as a bloc-forming move (reported in Al Jazeera, 14 Sep 2025). CAVEAT: this rests on state-media reaction reported in press summaries rather than on a doctrinal document, and reaction rhetoric is a weak proxy for an assessed threat ranking.

adversaryModel.statement: It appears to expect that the counterpart will absorb violence pitched below the threshold that would trigger general war and will prefer restoring the status quo to escalating — and, symmetrically, that conceding to an overwhelming demonstration of force is cheap when the leadership core itself is not the object of it.
adversaryModel.basis: INFERRED FROM AN OBSERVED PATTERN — this is the least document-anchored claim in the dossier and should be read as an analyst's reading, not as a statement the institution has made. Supporting record: after the August 1976 Panmunjom killings and the US-ROK show of force in Operation Paul Bunyan, the DPRK conveyed a statement of regret rather than escalating; the November 2010 Yeonpyeong shelling drew limited counter-battery fire and no wider response; the September 2020 killing of a South Korean official at sea was followed within days by a leadership-attributed apology transmitted through the United Front Department rather than by escalation on either side (Washington Post and RFA, 25 Sep 2020). Interpretive dispute is live and unresolved: V. Jackson, Rival Reputations: Coercion and Credibility in US-North Korea Relations (Cambridge UP, 2016), argues against the mechanical 'provocation cycle' framing in favour of a sustained rivalry in which both sides continually re-read each other's credibility; V. Cha & D. Kang, Nuclear North Korea: A Debate on Engagement Strategies (Columbia UP), stage exactly this inference as the point of disagreement. An engine should treat the belief as a distribution, not a constant.

declaredIdeology.statement: The organisation's own published programme is the Rules (Charter) of the Workers' Party of Korea as revised at the Eighth Congress, 5-12 January 2021: immediate goal, building a wealthy and civilised socialist society in the northern half of the Republic; final goal, a communist society. The revision deleted the 'National Liberation Democratic Revolution' clause and the Songun and pyongjin (byungjin) lines, cut most proper-noun references to past leaders, replaced 'the Party' with 'the Party Central Committee' throughout, strengthened the authority of the Party Central Military Commission and made the General Secretary its chairman, and fixed Congresses at five-year intervals.
declaredIdeology.basis: Hisashi Hirai (Kyodo News), 'On the Revisions to the Rules of the Workers' Party of Korea', Japan Institute of International Affairs Research Report, 9 Sep 2021 — a nine-point, clause-level account of the revision. CAVEAT, and it is the reason this is not marked high: the DPRK does not publish the Rules in full, so every clause-level reading including this one is reconstructed from state-media excerpts and copies obtained outside the country. The direction of the revision — more Party Central Committee, less Songun, less leader-name, stronger Central Military Commission — is corroborated across independent analyses; individual wordings are not independently verifiable. Recorded here strictly as what the organisation says about itself, with no inference drawn from it about any population.

history.episode: Bombing of Korean Air Flight 858 in flight between Abu Dhabi and Bangkok, killing all 115 aboard, by two agents who planted the device during the Abu Dhabi stopover and disembarked
history.choice: acted — a covert mass-casualty attack on a counterpart state's civil aviation, executed with a deniable method and denied at the time and since
history.lesson: Acted at the top of the harm range while paying for deniability — and this remains the last mass-casualty attack the institution has carried out against a counterpart state. `counterpartHarmRestraint` at 0.30 is therefore a floor read off an absence of repetition over nearly four decades, not off any documented targeting-restraint practice, and an engine should treat it as weakly supported in exactly that way.
history.basis: ROK investigation and the confession of the surviving agent; the US State Department concluded in January 1988 that the evidence of DPRK culpability was compelling and designated the DPRK a state sponsor of terrorism on that basis, a designation that stood until 2008 (Association for Diplomatic Studies and Training, 'North Korea Blows up South Korean Airliner', 2016, oral-history account). An earlier draft also cited a contemporaneous statement by the Assistant Secretary of State for Public Affairs in January 1988 with no name, title or document identifier; that citation was not checkable and has been removed. CAVEAT: a minority of ROK researchers dispute the investigation's findings, and the DPRK has never acknowledged the act; the international designation rests on the ROK investigation.

history.episode: First nuclear test at the Punggye-ri site near Kilju, announced as an intention six days beforehand and notified to its principal patron roughly twenty minutes in advance
history.choice: acted — proceeded over the stated objection of the only state supplying it with substantial economic support, and did so overtly
history.lesson: Acted without coalition and without concealment. The decision was not negotiated with the patron whose support it depended on, and the intent was announced rather than hidden — the earliest clean instance of the demonstration lane in which visibility is the product, and of a decision structure with no external or internal veto to route around.
history.basis: DPRK Foreign Ministry statement of intent, 3 Oct 2006; test conducted 9 Oct 2006 at 10:36 local time near Kilju. Advance notice to China of roughly twenty minutes, with a stated expected yield of about 4 kt against a measured yield widely assessed below 1 kt — Hui Zhang, 'North Korea's Oct. 9 Nuclear Test: Successful or Failed?', Belfer Center / INMM proceedings, 2007. UN Security Council Resolution 1718 followed on 14 Oct 2006. CAVEAT: the twenty-minute figure originates in contemporaneous US and ROK official briefings relayed through press reporting, not in any released primary document, and should be treated as approximately right rather than exact.

history.episode: Artillery shelling of Yeonpyeong Island — roughly 170 rounds onto an inhabited garrison island following an ROK live-fire drill conducted during the Hoguk exercise into waters the DPRK claims — killing two ROK marines and two civilian workers and wounding about nineteen
history.choice: acted, then stopped — struck above the level of the provocation against an inhabited target and halted without being compelled to
history.lesson: Escalated above the provoking act and then terminated. This is the clearest single observation of harm being calibrated rather than maximised, and it is the main OBSERVED support for `reciprocityProportion` at 0.68 under the parent profile's stated convention that higher means responding at or above the provocation level — a convention the profile itself flags as the largest interpretive risk it carries.
history.basis: 38 North, 'The Yeonpyeong Island Incident, November 23, 2010' (Jan 2011). The DPRK had warned in advance against the drill; the exchange followed. CAVEAT: whether the halt reflects a decision to stop or the effect of ROK counter-battery fire, weather and ammunition is not established in open sources, and both readings remain live — which is why this episode is offered as evidence of calibration, not of confident escalation control.

history.episode: Announced plan for 'enveloping fire' around Guam — four Hwasong-12 intermediate-range missiles overflying three named Japanese prefectures to land 30-40 km from the island — reviewed at the Strategic Force command and then not executed
history.choice: held — published a specific, numerically detailed strike plan, then declined to carry it out while explicitly keeping it available and ordering the force to stand ready
history.lesson: Held. The institution treated the announced plan as the instrument and the launch as optional, which is the demonstration lane operating at its purest: the product was the signal. It is also the cleanest evidence that the institution believes it can stop a sequence it has publicly started — belief, not demonstrated capability, and the parent profile's 0.55 on `escalationControlBelief` sits inside a live scholarly dispute for that reason.
history.basis: KPA Strategic Force commander's statement of 9-10 Aug 2017 setting out the plan in operational detail (North Korea Leadership Watch, 'KPA Strategic Force Issues Statement', 9 Aug 2017; BBC, 10 Aug 2017). KCNA report of 15 Aug 2017 that the leadership had examined the plan and would watch the counterpart's conduct further before deciding, with the force ordered ready should the decision be taken (BBC, 'N Korea leader briefed on Guam plan but opts to wait', 15 Aug 2017; Reuters and Al Jazeera, 15 Aug 2017). The plan was never executed; an unrelated Hwasong-12 overflight of Japan followed on 29 Aug 2017 on a different azimuth.

history.episode: Third Plenary Meeting of the Seventh Central Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea, which adopted a 'new strategic line', decided to suspend nuclear tests and ICBM launches, and announced dismantlement of the northern nuclear test ground
history.choice: held — restraint taken as a formal decision of a party organ, sustained for more than four years
history.lesson: Held, and held long. The institution can convert restraint into a resourced, announced line rather than an ad hoc pause, can hold an unspent capability for years, and will trade tempo for standing at head-of-state level. `legitimacyWeight` at 0.28 should be read as a discount on external approval rather than indifference to status — this decision was staged for an audience the institution wanted something from.
history.basis: Report on the Third Plenary Meeting of the Seventh Central Committee of the WPK, 20 Apr 2018 (KCNA text as republished by the National Committee on North Korea). The Punggye-ri test ground was demolished on 24 May 2018 in the presence of invited foreign journalists and with no technical verification. Duration: no nuclear test has followed to date and ICBM launches resumed in March 2022. CAVEAT: the freeze covered tests, not fissile-material production or shorter-range systems, dismantlement was unverified, and the site was assessed as partly restored from 2022 — the restraint is real and its scope was narrow.

history.episode: Second US-DPRK head-of-state summit in Hanoi, which ended abruptly with no agreement over the scope of a Yongbyon-for-sanctions-relief exchange
history.choice: refused — left a summit it had invested heavily in rather than accept terms that priced the retained capability, and absorbed continued sanctions as the cost
history.lesson: Refused and paid. The institution offered a facility and declined to go further, accepting a known and continuing economic cost over a deal touching the capability it had already declared settled. This is the observed behaviour behind the parent profile's `nuclear-capability-retention` redline — a case where the price of refusal was explicit, quantified by the counterpart, and paid anyway.
history.basis: The summit ended on 28 Feb 2019 with no joint agreement. Accounts of the terms conflict irreconcilably in open sources: the US side stated the DPRK sought relief from sanctions 'in their entirety'; the DPRK foreign minister's post-summit press conference in Hanoi stated the request was for partial relief in exchange for verifiable dismantlement of Yongbyon (CNN, 28 Feb 2019). Arms Control Association, 'Hanoi Summit Ends Abruptly: What's Next?', North Korean Denuclearization Digest, 6 Mar 2019; United States Institute of Peace, 'U.S.-North Korea Negotiations: What Happened in Hanoi?', Feb 2019. What is not in dispute: no agreement was signed, and the DPRK walked.

history.episode: Preliminary meeting for the Fifth Meeting of the Seventh Central Military Commission, which suspended the KPA General Staff's four-point military action plan against the ROK announced six days earlier
history.choice: held — a prepared and partly pre-positioned military action was deferred, explicitly not cancelled, by the ratifying body above the staff that proposed it
history.lesson: Held at the ratification gate. This is the only well-documented instance of a prepared DPRK military action being stopped by a named institutional body, and it demonstrates both halves of `decisionCentralization` at 0.94: staff can develop and begin pre-positioning without authorisation, and the authority to stop them sits in one place above them. It also shows the institution reserving a suspended plan rather than abandoning it.
history.basis: The KPA General Staff announced the four-point plan on 17 Jun 2020 (border force build-up and support for a leaflet operation). The Central Military Commission preliminary meeting of 23 Jun 2020 deferred it, reported by KCNA the following day (AP / Washington Post, 'N. Korea: Kim suspended military retaliation against South', 23-24 Jun 2020; Al Jazeera and Korea Times, 24 Jun 2020). 38 North, 'Kim Jong Un Puts Anti-South Korea Military Operation on Hold. What Now?' (25 Jun 2020), records that preparations for at least the leaflet campaign had begun before the meeting, and that the ROK military stayed on alert because the plans were suspended rather than cancelled. KCNA gave no reason. CONTEXT THAT CUTS AGAINST OVER-READING THIS: the hold came a week after the inter-Korean liaison office at Kaesong was demolished on 16 Jun 2020, so the institution had already acted destructively and then declined to go further — restraint at the margin, not instead of action.

history.episode: Theft of approximately $1.5 billion in virtual assets from the Bybit cryptocurrency exchange — the largest single cryptocurrency theft on record — followed by rapid conversion and dispersal across thousands of addresses on multiple blockchains
history.choice: acted — executed in the lane where effect without acknowledgement is the objective, and never claimed
history.lesson: Acted covertly, at a scale that would be a strategic act if it were claimed, and said nothing. The institution that publishes signed launch orders has never acknowledged a single attributed cyber operation. This is the observation that makes `attributionAversion` at 0.45 describe no behaviour the actor has shown: the honest encoding is roughly 0.8 in this lane and roughly 0.1 in the demonstration lane, and an engine that averages them will predict a middle behaviour that has never occurred.
history.basis: FBI Public Service Announcement, 26 Feb 2025 (IC3 PSA 250226), attributing the theft of approximately $1.5B from Bybit on or about 21 Feb 2025 to DPRK cyber activity the Bureau tracks as 'TraderTraitor', and describing rapid conversion to Bitcoin and dispersal across thousands of addresses. INSTITUTIONAL ATTRIBUTION rests on the prior chain, not on this PSA: CISA/State/Treasury/FBI Alert AA20-106A (rev. 23 Jun 2020) placing DPRK cyber actors under the Reconnaissance General Bureau; DOJ, '3 North Korean Military Hackers Indicted…' (C.D. Cal., unsealed 17 Feb 2021), charging three members of RGB units with a scheme to steal and extort more than $1.3 billion, building on the complaint unsealed 6 Sep 2018 against a programmer operating through a DPRK front company (Sony 2014, Bangladesh Bank 2016, WannaCry 2017). Scale context: MSMT (11 nations), 22 Oct 2025, assessing at least $1.65B stolen January-September 2025 and at least $1.19B in 2024. NOTE ON `proxyPreference`: what appears here is facilitation — front companies, laundering intermediaries, fabricated and stolen identities — not delegated decision authority, which is why 0.28 rather than a high value.

history.episode: Deployment of DPRK ground forces to Russia's Kursk region from October 2024, and the Central Military Commission's written acknowledgement of that deployment on 28 April 2025, two days after the partner state disclosed it
history.choice: acted, absorbed casualties assessed at up to half the deployed force, rotated replacements in, and only then claimed the deployment publicly
history.lesson: Acted and absorbed. Losses on that scale did not reverse the commitment; reinforcements followed. It also separates the attribution decision from the action decision inside the same institution — the deployment ran roughly six months unacknowledged and was then claimed through a Central Military Commission written statement framing it as a treaty obligation the apex office had determined was triggered, which is legitimation being harvested from a cost already paid.
history.basis: Treaty on Comprehensive Strategic Partnership signed at the Pyongyang summit of 18-19 June 2024 (sources differ on the signing date), ratified by both parties in November 2024 and in force from 4 Dec 2024; Article 4 commits each party to immediate military and other assistance by all available means, invoking UN Charter Article 51, if the other is subjected to armed aggression (CRS In Focus IF12760, 'Russia-North Korea Relations'; E. Howell, 'North Korea and Russia's dangerous partnership', Chatham House research paper, Dec 2024; CSIS, 'The New Russia-North Korea Security Alliance'). Acknowledgement: 38 North, 'North Korea's Acknowledgement of War Participation' (Apr 2025), describing the unusual Central Military Commission 'written stand' and the framing that the leadership determined the Kursk situation met the Article 4 criteria. CASUALTY FIGURES ARE CONTESTED AND SHOULD NOT BE STATED AS ONE NUMBER: UK Defence Intelligence assessed roughly 6,000 casualties from about 11,000 deployed by June 2025 (Bloomberg, 16 Jun 2025), while ROK assessments earlier in 2025 put the figure nearer 4,000 with roughly 3,000 reinforcements sent in January-February 2025; 38 North, 'North Korea's Military Intervention in Kursk: A High Casualty Learning Curve' (Feb 2025), documents tactical adaptation under those losses. Only the direction — continued rotation after heavy losses — is reliable.

weakestClaim.finding: confidence "low". It is the only claim in the dossier inferred from a behavioural pattern rather than read off a document the institution issued: the belief that the counterpart absorbs sub-threshold violence and prefers restoring the status quo is an analyst's reading of 1976 Panmunjom, 2010 Yeonpyeong and the Sept 2020 killing-plus-apology sequence, and the strategic-culture literature disputes exactly that inference (Jackson, Rival Reputations, 2016, against the mechanical "provocation cycle"; Cha vs. Kang staging it as the point of disagreement). It should be carried as a distribution, not a constant. Runner-up weaknesses: procedure.tempo (low — both clean crisis timelines are cases where the institution HELD, so the 5-7 day figure measures deliberation under scrutiny, not strike tempo) and procedure.steps[2] (low — OGD/General Political Bureau cadre-vetting mechanics rest on defector-derived reporting) and steps[6] (low — the lane split is well evidenced but assigning the attribution decision specifically to the Propaganda and Agitation Department is inferred, not documented).

profiles.label: Profit-motivated criminal syndicate
profiles.summary: Models a revenue-maximizing extortion enterprise organized as a licensing business: a small core sets pricing, tooling and rules while unaffiliated licensees choose targets, so authority is centralized over strategy and payment terms but decentralized over who gets hit. It optimizes tightly on the monetization subgame — revenue-scaled demands, staged deadlines, routine large discounts — and behaves opportunistically on target selection, taking whatever access a third-party market happens to sell; harm to noncombatants is a byproduct of coercive leverage rather than an objective, which is why restraint is near zero without the actor being a deliberate harm-maximizer. Normative legitimacy exerts no constraint at all, but the actor is acutely sensitive to anything that converts payment into an illegal act for the victim or resolves its principals to a legal person. Under enforcement pressure it absorbs little cost and prefers dissolution and rebranding to carrying the loss, while taking sharply more risk to hold its licensee labor base.

ownCostTolerance.basis: Profit-only objective; absorbed loss buys nothing. Observed: brands dissolve and rebrand rather than carry enforcement cost (Europol IOCTA 2025). Counter-evidence lowers confidence: DarkSide's May 2021 'our goal is to make money' statement was post-hoc damage control, not pre-emptive target avoidance, and LockBit's lead absorbed 18 months of degraded revenue and legal exposure to relaunch (Check Point, Q3 2025). Tolerance is low for operational cost, higher for reputational cost.

counterpartHarmRestraint.basis: OBSERVED targeting shows near-zero restraint: CISA/FBI AA23-165A lists education, government and emergency services, and healthcare among sectors attacked by LockBit affiliates. DECLARED exclusions exist and are unreliable (ALPHV voided all limits except the shelter jurisdiction in Dec 2023; DarkSide announced target vetting after Colonial). Consequence anchor, not a preference measure: McGlave, Neprash and Nikpay (AEJ: Economic Policy 18(1), 2026, 256-81) find in-hospital mortality rises 34-38% for patients already admitted when an attack begins. Confidence medium because harm is a byproduct of coercion pressure, not an observed objective.

attributionAversion.basis: Split construct: near-zero aversion to BRAND attribution (leak sites, press outreach and taunting are core to coercion) against high aversion to LEGAL-IDENTITY attribution. Behavioral evidence: persona/legal-identity separation, arrests concentrated on actors outside the shelter jurisdiction, and the May 2024 NCA/OFAC identification of LockBit's lead, after which the brand lost affiliate trust and access pricing collapsed. NOTE: the earlier $1M LockBit bounty is NOT evidence of aversion - it was an offer to pay for doxxing its own lead, and AA23-165A lists it under publicity stunts used to attract affiliates.

proxyPreference.basis: Surrogate execution is definitional to the model: the core licenses to 'unconnected affiliates' (CISA AA23-165A), initial access is bought from brokers (Chainalysis 2026: ~$14M IAB on-chain inflows in 2025), and laundering and hosting are outsourced to third-party providers (OFAC designations of Zservers Feb 2025, Aeza Jul 2025, Media Land Nov 2025).

escalationControlBelief.basis: The actor behaves as if coercive pressure is a dial it controls - staged deadlines, partial disclosure, and widening notification of third parties (Chainalysis 2026). Demonstrated control is worse than the belief: Colonial Pipeline and Kaseya produced state-level responses the actor did not anticipate or want. This parameter encodes the actor's BELIEF about controllability, which the record shows is overconfident.

timeHorizon.basis: Short at the operational layer, longer at the enterprise layer. Operational: Secureworks (2023) median ransomware dwell time just under 24h with deployment inside 5h in just over 10% of cases; Mandiant M-Trends 2026 median access-to-operator handoff of 22 seconds in 2025. Counter-evidence lowering the case for an extreme value: the same M-Trends edition reports overall median dwell time rising to 14 days in 2025; brands persist for years and rebuild after disruption (LockBit relaunch Sept 2025); retained exfiltrated data is held as a long-lived asset. Raised from 0.15 because the 22-second figure measures access-market liquidity, not the actor's planning horizon.

decisionCentralization.basis: CONTESTED and bimodal by decision type, so a single scalar is weakly identified. Ecosystem fragmentation is well evidenced (AA23-165A ties wide TTP variance to 'unconnected affiliates'; Chainalysis 2026 finds decreasing centralization and ~85 active extortion groups). But two peer-reviewed network studies of the same leaked Conti corpus (n=168,740) find a hierarchical, firm-like core with identifiable leadership and division of labor - Paternoster, Nazzari, Jofre and Uberti, Global Crime 26(2), 2025, 148-171, and Whelan et al., Global Crime 2025 (doi:10.1080/17440572.2025.2534387). Within a single syndicate, brand, pricing policy and rules are set centrally while target selection is delegated. Modelers should treat centralization as high for strategy and low for targeting.

lossFrameRiskAcceptance.basis: Under enforcement pressure the actor takes risk it otherwise avoids. Observed: after the Dec 2023 FBI action ALPHV declaratively abolished all targeting limits except the shelter jurisdiction and raised affiliate commissions to hold its labor base, then exit-scammed the affiliate on the ~$22M Change Healthcare payment (Krebs, Mar 2024). ASSUMED, not established: that the record-low 28% payment rate (Chainalysis 2026) causes harsher extortion; the reported rise in median payment is at least partly a composition effect as smaller victims stop paying.

legitimacyWeight.basis: Normative legitimacy - international law, alliance approval, legal cover - exerts no constraint on this actor's choices. Distinguish this from instrumental sensitivity to the victim's legal environment, which is high: sanctions designation is brand-damaging precisely because it converts payment into a legal act for the victim. That sensitivity belongs to cost and payment-channel variables, not to legitimacy. The binding reputational analogue - standing in the criminal labor market - is modeled separately.

signalingPreference.basis: Coercion requires credible visibility: leak-site publication, deadlines, proof-of-decryption credibility signals, and outreach to press, regulators and third parties (Meurs, Cartwright, Cartwright, Houba and Woods, Tinbergen TI 25-052/VII, 2025; Chainalysis 2026). Signaling is instrumental rather than expressive and can be dialed down when it serves revenue - the relaunched LockBit operation in Sept 2025 was observed running private victim portals without public listings (Check Point, Q3 2025).

reciprocityProportion.basis: Asymmetric rather than proportional. Escalation against a non-paying victim is a pricing instrument, not retaliation, and the negotiation literature finds de-escalation is at least as common: Sophos (2025) reports 53% of payers paid below the initial demand and payers averaged 85% of it, and Meurs et al. (2025) model large discounts as a standard stage. Against law enforcement the actor does not retaliate at all - it dissolves and rebrands. Lowered from 0.72 because the original basis conflated commercial escalation with reciprocity.

redlines.statement: Will not take any move that resolves its principals to a legal person or to seizable assets — no ransom figure buys exposure of legal identity, presence in an extradition-cooperative jurisdiction, or settlement through a rail that attributes funds to a named individual. Attribution to the BRAND is the opposite of constrained: leak-site publication, press outreach and taunting are core coercive instruments, so only legal-identity attribution is refused.
redlines.basis: Observed persona/legal-identity separation; arrests concentrated on actors who left the shelter jurisdiction; brand degradation following the May 2024 NCA/OFAC identification of a brand lead; enforcement pivot toward hosting and laundering providers rather than brands (OFAC designations: Zservers Feb 2025, Aeza Jul 2025, Media Land Nov 2025). Explicitly NOT based on the widely miscited $1M 'anti-doxxing bounty' — that was an offer to PAY for doxxing its own affiliate-program boss, listed in CISA/FBI AA23-165A among publicity-generating stunts.

redlines.statement: Does not conduct operations against targets inside the jurisdiction that shelters its principals — whichever jurisdiction that is. It is the only targeting rule that survived when a major brand publicly voided every other exclusion under maximum enforcement pressure in December 2023, and it is enforced through licensee agreements and by gating execution on shelter-jurisdiction system indicators rather than by any stated norm.
redlines.basis: Rules-of-conduct posting by one brand, 19-20 Dec 2023 (declaratory, corroborative only — this actor class lies in public postings); the load-bearing evidence is observed: arrest geography, licensee-agreement enforcement, and execution gated on shelter-jurisdiction system indicators (Mandiant, 2021). Recorded Future, Dark Covenant 3.0 (2025) characterizes the shelter as externally granted, selective, managed and revocable.

redlines.statement: Will not surrender the retained copy of exfiltrated data in any verifiable way, at any price. This is a commitment infeasibility rather than a value: no mechanism exists by which the actor could demonstrate deletion, so 'pay and the copy provably disappears' is never in its choice set, and a settlement that requires it cannot be reached.
redlines.basis: US government #StopRansomware victim guidance (payment does not guarantee deletion); the March 2024 episode in which a licensee retained the data after the core brand exit-scammed it on a ~$22M payment (Krebs, Mar 2024). The earlier 'retained data underwrites a future re-extortion revenue stream' rationale is dropped — the profile's own negotiation source reports no evidence that re-extortion is common, and that specific quote is itself unverified.

profiles.uncertainty:
**Only one of the three entries is an internalized commitment.** `principal-liberty-preservation` is the genuine redline: it does not respond to price and it explains the actor's behavior across payment channels, jurisdiction of residence, and operational security. The other two are included because they remove moves from the choice set, but for different reasons that a modeler must not conflate:

- `shelter-jurisdiction-nonaggression` is **externally imposed and conditional**, not a value. Recorded Future's *Dark Covenant 3.0* (events through Sept 2025) describes the shelter as selective, managed and revocable. That makes it a lever an intervention can move, unlike a values-based constraint. If the engine supports it, specify this as a hard filter with a small defection probability rather than an inviolable one, and re-evaluate if the host relationship is modeled as changing.
- `no-verifiable-data-deletion` is an **inability to commit**, not a refusal. It belongs in the choice set filter, but it should not be read as resolve.

**Two of the three carry `constraint: null`, and are therefore inert in the kernel.** The shelter commitment is a jurisdictional target filter and the deletion item is a settlement-form filter; neither is honestly expressible as a bound on civilianHarmShare, legitimacyCost, visibility or attributability. Forcing either into one of the four attributes would fabricate behavior. If the engine gains a target-jurisdiction attribute or a settlement-verifiability attribute, these two become live filters; until then they are documentation, and the shelter constraint in particular is the single most behaviorally consequential thing the current schema cannot represent.

**The one live number, `attributability: 0.2`, is the least defensible parameter here.** The construct is split: near-zero aversion to brand attribution against high aversion to legal-identity attribution, and the engine's single `attributability` axis ("traced to whoever ordered it") captures only the second. It is also weakened by the challenge pass: the claim that naming a brand's lead was fatal is **false** — that operation was severely degraded but relaunched in early Sept 2025 with 15+ distinct victims identified in Q3 2025 (Check Point). And the claim that the designation degraded the brand more than the infrastructure seizure is **contested**, not settled: Analyst1 attributes the licensee exodus to the seizure operation itself, with licensee access collapsing from ~$10,000 to ~$700. Public identification is therefore survivable, which argues the bound is a strong aversion near the edge of redline status rather than an absolute. Treat 0.2 as ±0.1 and expect the actor to still act when only brand exposure, not identity exposure, is at stake.

**No `compels_response` redline exists, and that is a finding.** Escalation against a non-paying victim is a pricing instrument, not retaliation — the negotiation literature shows de-escalation is at least as common (53% of payers paid below the initial ask; payers averaged 85% of demand, Sophos 2025). Against law enforcement the actor does not retaliate; it dissolves, rebrands, or relaunches. Any modeled tit-for-tat here would be an artifact.

**No ideological redline. This is the strongest negative finding in the profile.** No political, territorial or normative objective is protected; sector, victim identity, and any geography outside the shelter are all tradeable at price. The one brand that took a public political side in Feb 2022 suffered an insider leak of 168,740 internal messages — though its wind-down three months later was multi-causal (a costly campaign against one government, sanctions converting payment into a legal act, and dispersal into successor brands), not a clean consequence of the leak. Do not give this actor a values-based hard constraint.

**Sourcing corrections carried forward.** The government advisory's sector list is "education", not "K-12". The frequently quoted "we will now vet targets" statement from May 2021 is a post-hoc announcement of *future* vetting followed by brand exit, not evidence of pre-emptive target avoidance. The Conti structure study is Paternoster, Nazzari, Jofre & Uberti, *Global Crime* 26(2), 2025, 148-171 (doi:10.1080/17440572.2025.2473350) — the CrimRxiv posting is the preprint — and the "related" 2025 study is Whelan et al. on the same corpus, making **two** peer-reviewed studies finding firm-like hierarchy. The December 2023 rules posting should be cited to contemporaneous primary reporting, not to a vendor blog. Europol's "120+ brands" could not be verified and is in tension with the ~85 groups figure the profile also cites (different counting bases: leak-site identities vs. groups with observed on-chain payments) — reconcile or drop one.

**Essentialism.** The audit found none, and the profile is unusually clean. Two scoping fixes applied here: the shelter constraint is stated as a **variable** ("whichever jurisdiction that is") rather than pinned to a named region, so the engine encodes the mechanism — a protection relationship that can be withdrawn — rather than a geographic identity; and the evidence base is one licensing ecosystem under one permissive host jurisdiction, 2019-2026, used as the reference case for profit-motivated extortion. Presenting it as the universal archetype invites the misreading that the traits are national rather than structural.

**Scope boundary.** This is the pure profit-motivated case. A subset of real actors sits at the state-criminal boundary, with target selection responsive to another principal's interest and cost tolerance underwritten by protection — a different objective function that would change all three entries above. That case needs its own profile; do not stretch this one to cover it.

DarkSide's May 2021 post-Colonial statement ("We are apolitical… Our goal is to make money, and not creating problems for society"), and ALPHV's Dec 2023 rules statement, both as reported contemporaneously (Threatpost; Barracuda Networks blog, Mar 2024). Journalism, used only for the actors' own declaratory text.
profiles.declaredVsObserved: Declared licensee rules across several brands prohibited hospitals, schools, non-profits and critical infrastructure — a declared-doctrine reading would support harm restraint near 0.45 — while observed targeting includes education, healthcare, and government and emergency services, and one brand formally voided every such exclusion under enforcement pressure in Dec 2023, keeping only the shelter-jurisdiction rule; the declared exclusions function as licensee-recruitment marketing and reputational insurance rather than as enforced constraints, so the observed value (0.15) is the one encoded. The same gap appears in the frequently cited post-incident pledge to start vetting targets, which was a declaratory statement issued after the fact and followed by brand exit, not observed pre-emptive avoidance.

authority.statement: Go/no-go on which organisation is attacked sits with the licensee, not with the core. The core holds a near-monopoly over admission to the programme, the build pipeline, the leak site, the victim-negotiation portal, the price floor and the payment split, and it can expel a licensee after the fact; it does not select victims and in the dominant brands does not see a victim before deployment. Authority is therefore split by decision type — centralized over strategy, pricing and rails, delegated over targeting — which is why a single decisionCentralization scalar is weakly identified.
authority.basis: CISA, FBI, MS-ISAC and six partner agencies, Advisory AA23-165A, 'Understanding Ransomware Threat Actors: LockBit', 14 June 2023, attributes wide TTP variance directly to the 'large number of unconnected affiliates in the operation'. The 7 May 2025 dump of a LockBit affiliate-panel database (records 18 Dec 2024 - 29 Apr 2025) shows the core owning build generation, victim records, negotiation chat and a ~20% cut, plus per-affiliate registration fees — Trellix Advanced Research Center, 'Inside LockBit's Admin Panel Leak' (2025); TRM Labs, 'LockBit Leak Provides Insight into Ransomware-as-a-Service Enterprise' (2025). Principal counter-evidence for a more hierarchical reading: Paternoster, Nazzari, Jofre and Uberti, 'Inside the Leak: Exploring the Structure of the Conti Ransomware Group', Global Crime 26(2), 2025, 148-171, find a firm-like core with identifiable leadership in the leaked Conti corpus (n=168,740). Confidence held at medium because the split is read off two brands' internal data and Chainalysis (2026 Crypto Crime Report) counts ~85 active extortion brands, most of which have never been observed from the inside.

steps.office: The core programme's affiliate-recruitment function
steps.gate: Rejects applicants who cannot produce forum tenure, a positive reputation and a deposit. The filter is against researchers and law-enforcement infiltration, not against target choice — nothing at this stage constrains who a licensee will later attack. The threshold has risen since 2024 without the mechanism changing shape.
steps.basis: RAMP's published registration conditions on reopening, 13 Aug 2021, required an existing XSS or Exploit.in account with at least two months of history and positive reputation plus a registration fee reported at ~$500 (CloudSEK, 'The Rise and Fall of RAMP: Inside the Forum Where Ransomware Was Always Welcome', 2025; SOCRadar, 'Dark Web Forum: RAMP'). Recorded Future Insikt Group, 'Dark Covenant 3.0: Controlled Impunity and Russia's Cybercriminals' (2025), reports programme owners becoming more selective after Operation Endgame with the core mechanics intact and the entry threshold rising. Weakened by venue churn rather than by mechanism change: XSS.is was taken down in July 2025 and RAMP was seized by US authorities on 28 Jan 2026 (Rapid7, 'The Post-RAMP Era', 2026). All of this is industry reporting on closed forums, not a primary document. Authority chain as researched: operating through closed Russian-language crime forums

steps.office: The licensee's own operator team
steps.gate: Price and quality of the access on offer, not the identity of the organisation behind it. This stage is where the actor's opportunism is manufactured: the victim set for a given week is largely whatever the access market happened to be selling, which is the mechanism behind the profile's low rationalityPrecision.
steps.basis: Chainalysis, 2026 Crypto Crime Report (ransomware section), puts initial-access-broker on-chain inflows at ~$14M for 2025 with advertised access prices falling from ~$1,427 (Q1 2023) to $439 (Q1 2026). Mandiant, M-Trends 2026, reports a median initial-access-to-ransomware-affiliate handoff of 22 seconds in 2025, down from over eight hours in 2022 — a measure of market liquidity, not of the actor's planning horizon, and the profile's timeHorizon basis flags that misreading explicitly. Medium rather than high because neither source establishes what share of any single brand's victims arrive through purchased access as against self-developed intrusion. Authority chain as researched: purchasing from the third-party initial-access-broker market rather than developing access in-house

steps.office: The core's affiliate panel
steps.gate: Issues a target-specific build and key pair, and hard-codes the one filter this actor actually enforces before execution — an abort on shelter-jurisdiction system indicators. Nothing at this stage inspects the victim's sector, size or criticality.
steps.basis: Mandiant, 'Shining a Light on DARKSIDE Ransomware Operations' (2021), documents execution gated on a system-locale and keyboard-layout check that aborts on CIS systems — a targeting rule implemented in code rather than in policy, and the only one that survived when a major brand voided all other exclusions in Dec 2023. The leaked LockBit panel shows per-victim build generation for LockBit Black 4.0 and Green 4.0 across Windows, Linux and ESXi (Trellix, 2025). The development function is salaried rather than commission-based: US Department of Justice, 'United States Charges Dual Russian and Israeli National as Developer of LockBit Ransomware Group', press release and criminal complaint (D.N.J.), 20 Dec 2024, alleges ~$10,000 per month in cryptocurrency totalling more than $230,000 from June 2022 to February 2024 for malware development and consulting. Medium because the DOJ document is a charging allegation and the locale-check evidence is from one brand's tooling generalised across the class. Authority chain as researched: backed by a salaried in-house development function

steps.office: The licensee's operator team
steps.gate: Aborts or pivots where the environment can restore itself. Backup posture, not sector and not expected harm, is the decisive variable — the negotiation literature finds it the dominant determinant of whether a victim pays at all. Exfiltration completes here because the retained copy is the leverage that survives a successful restore.
steps.basis: Meurs, Cartwright, Cartwright, Houba and Woods, 'The Ransomware Pricing Paradox: An Empirical Study of the Six Stages of Ransomware Negotiations', Tinbergen Institute Discussion Paper TI 2025-052/VII (rev. Oct 2025), covering 481 police-reported incidents and 237 negotiation transcripts across 23 groups, finds backup status the dominant determinant of payment. Secureworks, State of the Threat (2023), reports median ransomware dwell time just under 24 hours with deployment inside five hours in just over 10% of cases. The abort behaviour is inferred from payment-determinant data rather than observed as an explicit decision in any recovered internal record, which caps confidence here. Authority chain as researched: with tooling and staging support drawn from the core's shared services

steps.office: The licensee, acting unilaterally
steps.gate: What is actually decided here is timing — off-hours, holidays, fiscal events — not eligibility. The one brand that announced a core-level pre-encryption approval gate announced it after the incident that prompted it and exited three days later, so the gate has never been observed operating on a live target.
steps.basis: DarkSide's 'About the latest news' posting, c. 10 May 2021: 'From today we introduce moderation and check each company that our partners want to encrypt to avoid social consequences in the future', followed by its 13 May 2021 announcement of lost infrastructure and brand exit — the actor's own declaratory text, reported contemporaneously (Vice/Motherboard, 10 May 2021; Axios, 14 May 2021), used for nothing but what it said. The profile's declaredVsObserved section records this as post-hoc announcement rather than observed pre-emptive avoidance. Timing selection: Cl0p's MOVEit mass exploitation was launched over the US Memorial Day weekend beginning 27 May 2023 (Kroll, 'Clop Ransomware: MOVEit Transfer Vulnerability CVE-2023-34362', June 2023). Authority chain as researched: core-level victim approval exists only as declared policy

steps.office: The core's victim-portal negotiation desk
steps.gate: Sets the opening demand against estimated victim revenue and bounds how far a licensee may discount. This gate stops nothing on harm grounds; what it stops is a licensee settling below the floor or off-platform.
steps.basis: Meurs et al. (TI 2025-052/VII, 2025) document a six-stage negotiation with revenue-scaled dynamic pricing and a high-demand-then-large-discount structure as standard practice rather than as failure. Sophos, The State of Ransomware 2025, finds 53% of payers paid below the initial demand, payers averaged 85% of it, and 71% of reductions were obtained through negotiation. The leaked LockBit panel carried the negotiation chat interface alongside victim records and the core's cut (Trellix, 2025). The existence of an enforced floor is inferred from the discount distribution and the panel's controls; no recovered pricing policy document states one, so this is the weakest-evidenced gate in the chain. Authority chain as researched: working to a core-set floor price and delegated discount authority

steps.office: The core's payment and publicity function
steps.gate: The only stage at which an external legal fact can stop the transaction: a sanctions designation touching the actor or its rail converts payment into an illegal act for the victim and removes the settlement from the choice set entirely. Note the inversion one major brand used — the licensee receives the payment first and remits the core's cut — which is a labour-market trust instrument, not a control.
steps.basis: CISA/FBI AA23-165A, 14 June 2023, records affiliates being paid before the core, an inversion of normal RaaS practice. US Treasury/OFAC designations of bulletproof-hosting providers Zservers (Feb 2025), Aeza Group (July 2025) and Media Land (Nov 2025) evidence the outsourced hosting and laundering layer and the enforcement pivot toward it. Trellix (2025) observes a ~20% core cut in the leaked panel, roughly $456,000 on ~$2.3M over five months. Chainalysis (2026) reports the payment rate at ~28%, an apparent all-time low, against a 50% rise in claimed attacks — most settlements now fail at this stage rather than earlier ones. Authority chain as researched: with laundering and hosting outsourced to third-party bulletproof providers

tempo.statement: Two clocks run, and they are commonly confused. The intrusion-to-encryption clock is hours to days and compressing; the negotiation clock is days to weeks and is the one the core actually manages. No stage in the chain requires an authorisation cycle longer than a chat message, so against this actor the defender's decision loop is usually the slower one — which is a statement about the absence of internal veto points, not about the actor's patience.
tempo.basis: Secureworks, State of the Threat (2023): median dwell just under 24 hours, deployment inside five hours in just over 10% of cases. Mandiant, M-Trends 2026: median initial-access-to-affiliate handoff of 22 seconds in 2025, while overall median dwell time rose to 14 days in the same edition — the two figures measure different things (access-market liquidity versus time resident in the network) and quoting the 22-second figure as a planning horizon is the specific error the profile's timeHorizon basis was rewritten to prevent.
